subject.title: Add native PowerShell smoke coverage for contributor commands

question: Should the native PowerShell smoke lane include both `pnpm check:docs` and `pnpm build:strict-smoke` now, or start with a smaller command set that already passes on Windows?
rationale: The direction fits OpenClaw test-infrastructure goals, but the active candidate changes recurring Windows runner work and currently fails in the requested build-smoke command.

options.title: Prove full smoke
options.body: Keep both requested commands in scope, but land only after `pnpm build:strict-smoke` is made Windows-safe and the exact `pwsh` lane passes.

options.title: Start narrower
options.body: Land native PowerShell coverage for already-passing contributor commands now and track Windows build-smoke separately.

options.title: Defer the lane
options.body: Keep the issue open while maintainers decide whether the recurring Windows runner cost is worth adding.

recommendation.title: Prove full smoke
recommendation.body: Keep both requested commands in scope, but land only after `pnpm build:strict-smoke` is made Windows-safe and the exact `pwsh` lane passes.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the strongest recent overlap across the current Windows CI matrix and adjacent PowerShell-safe docs tooling.
